To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Developmental conductive hearing loss impairs detection of a tonal signal masked by simultaneous noise.

early auditory deprivation in animals results in increased thresholds for detecting signals in noise and this is associated with reduced tone-evoked cortical responses in the presence, but not the absence, of noise.

(1) animals raised with CHHL have increased thresholds for detecting a tone in simultaneous noise, (2) intracellular recordings in the auditory cortex of control animals reveal a cortical correlate of masking, and (3) these results raise the possibility that altered neural processing which occurs with early CHL may contribute to the detection deficits in noise observed in SNHL listeners.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the central auditory system in signal detection in noise, a basic perceptual process that has important implications for speech perception in noise.
the role of the central auditory system in processing complex acoustic signals.
the mechanisms underlying signal detection deficits in listeners with hearing loss.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanisms underlying simultaneous maskers are not limited to the cochlea, but include cortical processing.
the mechanisms of simultaneous masking in noise are both peripheral and central.
both peripheral and central factors contribute to the increased simultaneous masking in listeners with hearing loss.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
developmental hearing loss impairs detection in noise, and that this impairment may be due to altered central mechanisms.
developmental auditory deprivation alters the central auditory system in ways that affect even simple signal detection.
early auditory deprivation alters central auditory processing in the brain, which may underlie the increased difficulty of signal detection in noise.

the central auditory system is involved in signal detection in noise, even for a simple task such as detecting a pure tone in broadband noise.
